anchor: a protection-set state element as updated by the most recently committed instruction
comment: No model updates the protection set only up to the last committed instruction. last_committed_protset_p applies the update rule to every instruction in spo order, committed or not. STT's rule removes the memory read by any load with no older unresolved branch. The commit-based rule is commented out. The dataflow figure caption already states the resolution-based rule, so the text and that caption disagree.
proposed: a data-dependence path from a protection-set state element (after the defense's update rule has been applied along speculative program order) to a leaked operand of a transmitter, ...
evidence: STAGE1_alloy/models/STT_6.als:232-243 (fold over f..f.spo^6), :329-331 (rule), :330 (commit rule commented out); tikz/dataflow_8pt.tex caption

anchor: These constraints are defense-agnostic.
comment: The models do not share all well-formedness facts. rf_from_most_recent_writer is in STT_6 but missing from Recon_6 and SPT_6_oneLP. SPT_6_oneLP also changes skeleton functions to an operand-typed protection set. URGENT_TODO.md:31 already has this as an open DECIDE. The text must match the decision. The figure's '1. Defense-agnostic execution well-formedness' has the same problem.
proposed: These constraints are shared by our defense models, with the per-model exceptions listed in Section~\ref{...}.
evidence: STT_6.als:161-169 vs diff of Recon_6.als / SPT_6_oneLP.als (fact absent); SPT_6_oneLP.als:220-265; URGENT_TODO.md:31

anchor: require our execution to violate the predicate (i.e. be an example of leakage)
comment: For SPT the generator asks for more than a violation. SPT_6_oneLP replaces 'not secure' with one_insecure_speculation_scheme_p: there must be exactly one leaking operand.
proposed: require our execution to violate the predicate (i.e. be an example of leakage; for SPT, at exactly one leaking operand)
evidence: SPT_6_oneLP.als:268-274, 313-314 (gen_useful_litmus)

anchor: \textbf{RC}: shift commit: flip last-uncommitted instruction to committed
comment: The code applies RC to the first uncommitted instruction, the one right after the commit boundary. 'Last-uncommitted' reads as the youngest instruction. RC is also never used alone: it is tested together with RR on that same instruction. When nothing is committed, first_uncommitted falls back to the first instruction.
proposed: \textbf{RC}: shift commit: mark the first uncommitted instruction (the commit boundary) committed and resolved
evidence: STT_6.als:306-308 (secure[RC->first_uncommitted + RR->first_uncommitted]), :139 (fallback to first_instr)

anchor: Rather than fix these stalls, we sweep them so that a reported leak is shown not to hinge on any single window setting
comment: The code does the reverse. A test is reported as leaking if any grid point triggers (OR over the sweep), so a reported leak can depend on a single setting. The per-point outcomes are saved in the *_sweep.json sidecars (triggered_points), so robustness could be reported, but the verdict does not mean that.
proposed: We sweep these stalls and report a test as leaking if any setting triggers it; per-setting outcomes are kept, so for each leak we also report how many settings trigger it.
evidence: pipeline.py:330-339 (comment: 'aggregates per-test as OR over grid points'), :500-558 (_aggregate_sweep_results: any_hit, triggered_points)

anchor: No cache or defense code is instrumented to \emph{see} a leak, only to \emph{realize} the scenario
comment: SimSpect does add instrumentation whose only job is observation. It adds print-only BR predict/resolve lines in bpred, IEW and commit on all 8 hooked builds, and cache, TLB and buffer event prints in the Ruby and classic cache code of the InvisiSpec, CleanupSpec and SpecLFB builds. The resolve hooks also change behaviour: the release now wakes the CPU. Also in this paragraph: O3PipeView prints fetch-to-retire ticks but no squash ticks. Squash ticks come from LSQUnit and Commit.
proposed: Observation hooks are print-only: they add trace lines (branch prediction and resolution, and on the footprint builds cache and buffer events), verified to leave the rest of the trace unchanged; no defense logic is modified.
evidence: wiki/design/RESOLUTION_HOOKS.md sec.1 (BR lines; edit 4 wakeCPU); wiki/design/SIMSPECT_HOOKS.md header; gem5-hooks/README.md table; STAGE3_gem5/gem5_common.py:455-477 (parse_pipeview fields)

anchor: The signal is the load's cache touch --- the tick at which its access reaches the cache
comment: check_ld times the load by its latest LSQ 'Executing load' tick. That tick fires at the top of the load path, before the defense decides whether to send the access, and the pipeview complete tick is the fallback. The packet and spec_read ticks only feed the yes/no data-obtained gate and are never compared with the window. The memaccess (SpecLFB) and expose (InvisiSpec) ticks belong to separate per-build checkers, not to this predicate.
proposed: The signal is the tick at which the LSQ executes the load (\texttt{Executing load}; \texttt{O3PipeView} \texttt{complete} if absent), and the load counts only if it then obtained data ...; the footprint builds use their own access ticks.
evidence: STAGE3_gem5/check_ld.py:30-37, 39-52, 85-87, 130-146; check_ld_speclfb.py:59-75; check_ld_invisispec.py:21-28

anchor: A resolved branch is generated only as correctly predicted and not taken
comment: There is one exception. The transmitter branch is always emitted as br_bez: architecturally taken, forced to mispredict, and given a resolve stall of 0, whatever its Alloy resolved flag. Table row 5 says this but the text does not.
proposed: A resolved branch is generated only as correctly predicted and not taken; the transmitter branch is the exception and is always mispredicted (Table~\ref{tab:instrtable}, row~5).
evidence: STAGE2_compilation/parsexml.py:738-776 (xm override); pipeline.py:404-421 (_inject_stalls: xmit stall 0)

anchor: Each chosen instruction is emitted as an inline-assembly block with a global PC label
comment: Two qualifications. Branches are not picked at random: pass 2.5 rewrites every non-transmitter branch to br_cond and the transmitter to br_bez. Also, for a branch only the condition set-up is inline asm with the PC label. LLVM emits the compare and the jcc, so LLVM's block layout decides which jcc direction is the speculative path. That is why the harness derives the forced direction from the binary.
proposed: Each chosen instruction is emitted as an inline-assembly block with a global PC label (for a branch, the label sits on the inline-asm condition set-up and LLVM emits the compare and jump)
evidence: STAGE2_compilation/parsexml.py:789-795 (branch rewrite), :2426-2427 and :2484 (icmp + br emitted by LLVM); wiki/design/RESOLUTION_HOOKS.md sec.2

anchor: interleaving builds transmitters fed by two independent speculative sources, which no single Alloy instance can express
comment: This is a capability, not something the evaluated corpus shows. A merge needs a backbone ALU op with an open input on the transmitter's path. In the STT_6 corpus every load transmitter's address is fed directly by one load, with 0 through an ALU op, and 99.6% of transmitters have in-degree 1. A backbone load's unspecified address is never emitted. It is the evaluated models' minimality, not Alloy, that excludes these merges: STT_6_multisource admits them. The interleave figure's base instance needed a forcing predicate.
proposed: interleaving can build transmitters fed by two independent speculative sources, which our minimal backbones exclude, when the backbone has an ALU op with an open input on the transmitter's path
evidence: wiki/findings/mdsToRead/OTB_GENERATION_GAP.md (TL;DR; re-checked 0/2000 fresh); ENUMERATION_OVERSPECIFICATION.md table; STAGE2_compilation/parsexml.py:2146; specs/alloy_models.json:53; tikz/interleave_v4_8pt.tex:7-9 (comment)

anchor: draw every unspecified operand from the shared free pool, the same pool the interleaved chains use
comment: Only unspecified register operands share the pool. Each unspecified memory operand gets a fresh, never-aliased slot. An unspecified address register of a load or store is not emitted: a constant offset is used instead. Without interleaving, the pool holds no chain registers.
proposed: draw every unspecified register operand from the shared free pool, the same pool the interleaved chains use (unspecified memory operands get fresh, unaliased slots)
evidence: STAGE2_compilation/parsexml.py:1601 (pass3: fresh mem slot), :2146 (pass5: only rf-specified inaddr used), pass_interleave returns empty pools when disabled

anchor: Instructions carry $\mu$arch flags for committed/resolved status, enforced in simulation to replicate execution.
comment: Only resolution is actively enforced, by the branch force, resolve stall and STL hold. Commit status is measured, not enforced. The evaluated fixed configs set the fnc commit stall to 0, and the checkers only require lc to retire and the signal to come before fnc retires. The Gem5 section says this correctly ('passively measuring').
proposed: Instructions carry $\mu$arch flags for committed/resolved status; resolution is enforced in simulation and commit status is checked against the trace.
evidence: runconfigs/fixed_20261030/*.jsonc (fnc_commit_stall_cycles 0); STAGE3_gem5/check_ld.py:95-114

anchor: Divide: unguarded, so a zero divisor faults.
comment: No evaluated model can produce an Other_x transmitter. Otherxs is commented out of the leakage function in STT_6, Recon_6 and SPT_6_oneLP, and tag_xm requires the xmit to own a leakage-function operand. So this row, check_other.py and the divide-fault promotion never ran in the reported campaigns. The same applies to pipeline.tex's 'Faulting / long-latency other transmitter' bullet.
proposed: (caption) ... Other\_x rows are supported by the pipeline, but no evaluated defense model lists Other\_x as a transmitter.
evidence: STT_6.als:327-328, Recon_6.als:320, SPT_6_oneLP.als:344 (leakage_function); STT_6.als:270-273 (tag_xm); STAGE3_gem5/gem5_common.py:772-852; OTB_GENERATION_GAP.md ('no other_x transmitters in any STT_6 testset')

anchor: Only the defense block (speculation contract, protection set, leakage function) differs between models.
comment: The vocabulary is shared, but more than the defense block differs. Recon_6 and SPT_6_oneLP lack rf_from_most_recent_writer. SPT_6_oneLP rewrites skeleton code: operand-typed a and last_committed_protset_p, secure_speculation_scheme_p, tag_xm, and an exactly-one-leak-point run predicate. Recon_6 changes a skeleton call site to hardware_protection_policy[p]. This is open as a DECIDE in URGENT_TODO.md:31.
proposed: The defense block (speculation contract, protection set, leakage function) is what defines each defense; the models also differ in a few skeleton facts (Section~\ref{...}).
evidence: diff STT_6.als vs Recon_6.als (rf fact; :229) and vs SPT_6_oneLP.als (:220-284, 313-314); URGENT_TODO.md:31

anchor:
\textbf{Protection set:}
All memory
comment: This omits STT's update rule, although the model section says every protection set comes with one. In STT_6, a load with no older unresolved branch removes the memory it reads from the protection set. The dataflow figure caption already states this rule.
proposed: All memory; a load with no older unresolved branch removes the location it reads from the protection set.
evidence: STAGE1_alloy/models/STT_6.als:326 (Mem_s), :329-331 (prot_set_propagation_p); sections/model.tex line 9

anchor: We have expressed seven hardware defenses and their variants in the \toolname{} language; STT, SpecShield, NDA, DoM, SPO, SPT, and ReCon
comment: Only STT, SPT and ReCon have current models. SpecShield and NDA exist only as commented-out blocks in archived models on an older skeleton. No DoM or SPO model exists. SpecLFB, InvisiSpec and CleanupSpec reuse STT_6. PAPER_PLAN.md (G6) already notes this, but the text still says seven.
proposed: We have expressed STT, SPT and ReCon and their variants in the \toolname{} language, and reuse the STT specification for SpecLFB, InvisiSpec and CleanupSpec
evidence: STAGE1_alloy/models/MANIFEST.md ('Current model per defense'); models/old_models/no_RI_add_spacers.als:392-435 (commented SpecShield/NDA); grep: no DoM/SPO .als; specs/defense_units.json units 4,6,7; PAPER_PLAN.md:73, :210

anchor: only 15\% percent of AMuLeT's randomly synthesized tests even contain the basic components necessary for leakage
comment: The repo figure for this claim is 17% (85 of 500 tests contain a leakable gadget). 15% is a different number: tests-to-detection, 6 vs 39. 'percent' after '\%' is also doubled.
proposed: only 17\% of AMuLeT's randomly synthesized tests even contain the basic components necessary for leakage
evidence: wiki/results/PAPER_RESULTS.md:42-45, :352-360 (sec.5); PAPER_PLAN.md:53, :58

anchor: uncover significant, previously unknown bugs in \emph{both} comprehensive defenses that we test---STT and SPT
comment: The repo does not yet support a separate SPT bug. defense_units says SPT-Fence shows the same race as STT with no SPT bug of its own, and PAPER_PLAN G4 says the SPT claim can't be written until EXP-4. The STT race appears only under slow commit-to-IEW timing (0 at stock). The intro repeats the claim ('shared by STT and SPT'). Meanwhile the ReCon store-forward bypass is a confirmed real bug and the abstract and intro omit it.
evidence: specs/defense_units.json unit 3 notes; PAPER_PLAN.md:208 (G4); wiki/findings/bug/BUGS.md (STT VP-squash race: slow-comm only; recon_SLF_stlf_bypass: REAL, confirmed 2026-11-03)

anchor: Stage~3 runs them on the defense's gem5 build under a non-invasive harness
comment: The harness changes prediction and timing on purpose. It forces branch directions, holds branch resolution and store addresses, and on the resolve-hook builds wakes the CPU at release. Only the defense logic is untouched. The same word appears in the figure body and in pipeline.tex ('non-invasively instrument'). The wording is an open item in URGENT_TODO.md:44.
proposed: Stage~3 runs them on the defense's gem5 build under a minimal harness that leaves the defense logic untouched
evidence: wiki/design/RESOLUTION_HOOKS.md sec.1 (behaviour changes; edit 4); gem5-hooks/README.md (STL hooks); paper_figures/plans/BIGFIG_FACT_AUDIT.md row 30; URGENT_TODO.md:44

anchor: for several defenses we maintain both the raw and the intersected execution contract
comment: Unsupported. Every evaluated model uses the same branch-only contract (uncommitted & has_unresolved_brs). The only alternative contracts are STT_6_futuristic, which is written but not reviewed or run, and STT_6_stl for stores. No defense has both a raw and an intersected contract in use.
proposed: for STT we have also written the broader Futuristic contract
evidence: STT_6.als:325, SPT_6_oneLP.als:337, Recon_6.als:315; STT_6_futuristic.als:368; wiki/design/FUTURISTIC_MODEL.md (status line)
